tracking.name: Fair-Ton / Tonelada Justa
tracking.description: Fair-Ton quantifies and scales GHG avoided emissions from waste pickers' inclusive recycling across Latin America, Asia, and Africa, producing high-quality MRV data to advance Paris-aligned climate action, climate justice, and waste sector mitigation.
tracking.indicator: Adoption of the Fair-Ton Measurement, Reporting and Verification (MRV) methodology by 100 waste picker organizations
tracking.findings: The published 2025 baseline of 34 is retained provisionally, pending validation of adoption criteria and the final calculator inventory. The inventory has 40 organization IDs for 2024 and 23 for 2025 (22 Brazil, 1 Bolivia). Twenty-two IDs recur, leaving 41 distinct IDs across both years; only one ID is new in 2025.

tracking.name: Global Alliance of Subnational Development Banks
tracking.description: The Global Alliance of Subnational Development Banks is strengthening SDBs for localizing climate agendas by building institutional capacity, fostering cooperation between SDBs, NDBs, and MDBs, and enhancing SDBs’ recognition in international climate finance frameworks.
tracking.indicator: 100% of member SDBs/NDBs aligning strategies with the climate SDGs and/or Paris Agreement by 2028
tracking.findings: Based on available data from 41 of the Alliance’s 57 member SDBs/NDBs, 33 institutions (58% of members of the Global Alliance) reported partial or full alignment with the Paris Agreement and/or climate-related SDGs. Other responses indicated indirect or no alignment, or that alignment had not yet been assessed. As not all the Alliance’s members reported or disclosed relevant information, this does not capture the full level of alignment across the Alliance.

tracking.name: Global Alliance of Subnational Development Banks
tracking.description: The Global Alliance of Subnational Development Banks is strengthening SDBs for localizing climate agendas by building institutional capacity, fostering cooperation between SDBs, NDBs, and MDBs, and enhancing SDBs’ recognition in international climate finance frameworks.
tracking.indicator: 1000 identified Local and Regional Governments (LGRs) supported by member SDBs/NDBs on climate projects by 2028
tracking.findings: Based on available data from 17 of the Alliance’s 57 member SDBs/NDBs that responded to this reporting question or publicly disclosed relevant information, 563 Local and Regional Governments were supported on climate-related projects in the 2025 fiscal year. This figure reflects reported support from participating members in Africa and LAC. As the Alliance represents only part of the global SDB landscape, it does not capture the full scale of LRGs supported by SDBs on climate projects worldwide.

tracking.name: Global Alliance of Subnational Development Banks
tracking.description: The Global Alliance of Subnational Development Banks is strengthening SDBs for localizing climate agendas by building institutional capacity, fostering cooperation between SDBs, NDBs, and MDBs, and enhancing SDBs’ recognition in international climate finance frameworks.
tracking.indicator: 500 million USD of urban climate finance mobilized through member SDBs/NDBs and tracked by Alliance
tracking.findings: Based on responses from 5 —ADM, BDMG, BRDE, FINDETER, and INFIVALLE— of the Alliance’s 57 member SDBs/NDBs to this reporting question, USD 308 million in urban climate finance was mobilized over the 2025 fiscal year. This figure reflects reported financing from participating members in Africa and Latin America and the Caribbean. As the Alliance represents only part of the global SDB landscape, it does not capture the full scale of urban climate finance mobilized by SDBs worldwide.

tracking.name: RegionsAdapt
tracking.description: Subnational governments are better equipped to lead ambitious climate adaptation, strengthening resilience and protecting vulnerable communities, while regional leadership, experiences and lessons shape and advance the Global Climate Action Agenda.
tracking.indicator: Supporting subnational governments assess, plan, act and report on climate adaptation.
tracking.findings: Since 2015, RegionsAdapt has grown from just 13 states and regions with adaptation plans or strategies to 59 today. While some members are only beginning their journey, others are already advancing into second and third iterations of their plans. Accountability is also a defining feature of the initiative: since RegionsAdapt joined the Race to Resilience, 46 members have been regularly reporting their progress, showing both ambition and delivery on the path towards our target of 100 regions.

cases.title: Strengthen Subnational Development Banks’ (SDB) access to Global Climate Fund (GCF) Locally Led Climate Action and Readiness
cases.initiative: by the Global Alliance of Subnational Development Banks
cases.target: Related CCI targets: 100 per cent of member SDBs/NDBs aligning strategies with the climate SDGs and/or PA by 2028; 1000 identified LGRs supported by member SDBs/NDBs on climate projects by 2028; USD 500 Million of urban climate finance mobilized through member SDBs/NDBs and tracked by Alliance
cases.contribution: This action is reported as contributing to Objective 13. Resilient urban development, mobility, and infrastructure, and Objective 20. Climate, sustainable and adaptation finance, mainstreaming climate in investments and insurance (under Axis 6).
body: In May 2026, the Global Fund for Cities Development (FMDV) hosted a technical dialogue in collaboration with the GCF through the Global Alliance of SDBs (African Chapter) and the Alliance of African Ministers for Urbanization Financing (AMUF) on the GCF Locally Led Climate Action framework. The session brought together 49 participants from 21 countries and 33 ministries, financial institutions and territorial organizations to discuss GCF Readiness, Financial Management Capacity Assessment (FMCA) requirements and national pathways for localizing climate finance.

The action contributed to building continental awareness and momentum around locally led climate finance, moving the discussion from general interest in accessing international climate finance toward a clearer understanding of the institutional arrangements required at national level. By connecting SDBs, ministries, National Designated Authorities (NDA) and GCF expertise, it strengthened the capacity of African institutions to explore Readiness support and develop more coherent national frameworks linking international climate finance with territorial implementation.  In the longer term, this supports the Alliance’s objective of positioning SDBs as key intermediaries able to connect global climate-finance mechanisms with local and regional governments, investment pipelines and climate-resilient territorial development. Importantly, the meeting established a direct channel for continued technical dialogue between GCF experts, African SDBs and national institutions.

cases.title: Opening a Fair Ton workstream in Mesoamerica with AECID
body: During September 2025 – August 2026, Fair Ton opened a Mesoamerican workstream with the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID) and regional partners. Its purpose is to adapt the initiative’s waste-picker data and MRV approach beyond the countries where it was first developed, while preserving the role of local organizations in producing and governing their information.

In June 2026 the team established coordination and defined a sequence: characterize participating organizations and their existing records, adapt diagnostic instruments, and identify the support needed for reliable data collection. In July it prepared assessment tools designed for replication across countries, drawing on lessons from Brazil and Chile. Toward the end of the period, a first regional meeting brought together participants from four Mesoamerican countries to discuss starting conditions and a common path for data governance. This work links Fair Ton’s objective of territorial scale to a practical process for understanding each local context before applying the MRV method.

This action tests whether a waste-picker-led measurement approach can scale through a network of local organizations rather than a single centralized data source. Standardized diagnostic tools and shared data-governance principles can help future cohorts enter the system with comparable information and control over their own records. The immediate contribution is institutional reach and readiness, measurable MRV adoption, material recovery and climate outcomes depend on subsequent documented reporting.

cases.title: RegionsAdapt Communities of Practice
body: RegionsAdapt advanced trilingual peer learning and capacity-building through two Communities of Practice sessions: one on Subnational Adaptation Finance, (April 2025) and another Strengthening Municipal Climate Adaptation through Regional Action (June 2026). In addition, a dedicated preparation webinar in September 2025 equipped members with insights and strategies ahead of COP 30.

Subnational governments are better equipped to accelerate and scale climate resilience by improving access to finance, strengthening multilevel governance, and sharing effective adaptation approaches across regions and municipalities.

Through this action, regional governments increased their capacity to identify and mobilize adaptation finance, strengthen collaboration with municipalities, and translate international climate discussions into practical subnational adaptation action.

The RegionsAdapt Communities of Practice contributes to the UNFCCC multilateral process by capturing how regional governments support the implementation of both the Paris Agreement, in alignment with the Global Goal on Adaptation.
